speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are a pediatric patient presenting with hypertension; can you tell me if you have experienced any headaches, blurred vision, or swelling in your legs recently?

speaker: Patient
text: 5-year-old boy. The patient is presented by his mother for a well-child visit. The boy was born at 39 weeks gestation via spontaneous vaginal delivery, is currently up to date on all vaccines, and is meeting all developmental milestones. His mother reports that he has been generally doing well with no concerns. No family history of cardiovascular disease. The boy does not take any medications.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for those details. Since his blood pressure is elevated at this young age, I need to determine if this is primary hypertension or secondary to an underlying condition. Did you notice any snoring, pauses in breathing during sleep, or excessive daytime sleepiness? Please also confirm his current height and weight percentile so we can assess for growth abnormalities.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is High blood pressure on the right upper extremity. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Migraine and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: It seems there has been some confusion; a 5-year-old boy typically does not present with migraines as the primary cause of isolated right upper extremity hypertension. The discrepancy in blood pressure between arms is a critical finding that suggests an issue with the subclavian artery or the aorta. Can you clarify if the elevated reading was confirmed by a second measurement, and have you noticed any pain in his right arm or leg? REQUEST TEST: Upper extremity blood pressure comparison and lower extremity blood pressure.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Blood Pressure Right Upper Extremity: 150/80 mm Hg; Blood Pressure Differential: Upper Extremities 150/80 mm Hg (Right), Compared to lower values in lower extremities; Echocardiogram Findings: Narrowing of the aorta distal to the left subclavian artery with a gradient, consistent with coarctation; Left ventricular function normal; Chest X-ray: Normal heart size, rib notching not observed.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Coarctation of the Aorta. The confirmed blood pressure differential between the upper and lower extremities, combined with echocardiographic evidence of aortic narrowing distal to the left subclavian artery, is diagnostic. No further testing is required at this time.
